content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"It treats Matthew 1:20 as UNDERDETERMINED because two competing senses/answers appear, which triggers the rule's bar on treating a two-sense verse as open.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"Phrase 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand': I weighed whether covenant-presence and physical-source are two senses that must both stand, barring UNDERDETERMINED, or merely opposing party answers to one link, allowing underdetermination.","why":"The judge's stated basis is that each side gave a reading of the conception in Matthew 1:20, so it marks the verse UNDERDETERMINED even though K-S2 says a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand."}
